questions.title: Adjacency Matrix Row
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (input reading and adjacency building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def matrix_row(adj, V, u):

adj is an adjacency dict keyed 0..V-1 for an UNDIRECTED graph and u is a vertex. Build row u of the adjacency matrix: a list of V entries where entry v is 1 when v is adjacent to u and 0 otherwise. The harness prints the row space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E — vertex count and edge count.
Next E lines: u v — an undirected edge (stored both ways).
Last line: the vertex u.

Output Format:
One line with V entries (0/1), space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50
0 <= E <= 30
0 <= u, v < V; no self-loops

questions.title: Fewest Hops Between Terminals
questions.description:
A packet grid routes hop by hop along links. The fewest-hops distance between two terminals is found by a breadth-first sweep that expands whole levels: level 1 holds the origin's neighbors, level 2 their new neighbors, and so on. If the target never appears, the terminals are disconnected — report -1. No imports — pure Python only.

The program scaffolding (input reading and adjacency building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_hops(adj, start, target):

adj is the adjacency dict keyed 0..V-1. Return the number of edges on the shortest path from start to target, 0 when they are the same vertex, -1 when target is unreachable.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E — terminal count and link count.
Next E lines: u v — a link (stored both ways).
Last line: start and target.

Output Format:
One line with the fewest-hops distance, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50
0 <= E <= 30
0 <= start, target < V

questions.title: Broadcast Order (BFS)
questions.description:
When a network alert fires, the switch with the alert fans the message out hop by hop: every switch that first receives it relays to its unvisited links immediately — a breadth-first sweep. Network ops replays the exact order in which switches receive the alert. No collections/deque — use a plain list as the queue with pop(0).

The program scaffolding (input reading and adjacency building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def bfs_order(adj, start, out):

adj is the adjacency dict keyed 0..V-1 (neighbors in input order) and start is the origin switch. Fill out with the BFS visit order and leave it to the harness to print. Neighbors must be explored in stored order.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E — switch count and link count.
Next E lines: u v — a link (stored both ways).
Last line: the origin switch start.

Output Format:
One line with the BFS order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50
0 <= E <= 30
0 <= start < V

questions.title: Depth Survey (Recursive DFS)
questions.description:
A survey crawler dives DEEP along each link before backtracking — a recursive depth-first sweep that visits neighbors in stored order. Loops over a frontier are banned (no while): the traversal must be recursive.

The program scaffolding (input reading and adjacency building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def dfs_order(adj, start, out):

adj is the adjacency dict keyed 0..V-1 (neighbors in input order) and start is the entry vertex. Fill out with the recursive DFS visit order (the visit of a vertex is recorded when it is first reached, before diving into its neighbors). The harness prints the filled list.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E — vertex count and edge count.
Next E lines: u v — an edge (stored both ways).
Last line: the entry vertex start.

Output Format:
One line with the DFS order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50
0 <= E <= 30
0 <= start < V
